question: What do the sources say about whether longer context windows alone guarantee better multi-document answer completeness?
required_claim: Longer windows do not guarantee complete evidence use; middle evidence can be missed.

passages.text: Tokenizers split text into subword units. Byte-pair encoding is common in modern LLMs.
GPU memory bandwidth often limits throughput before raw parameter count does.
Synthetic note C: When relevant sentences were placed in the middle of a long prompt, models more often failed to use them despite the full text fitting in the context window.
Beam search and sampling are decoding strategies; temperature controls randomness.
Retrieval indices can be built with dense embeddings or sparse lexical features.
Synthetic note D: Answer fluency can remain high even when only a subset of required evidence items is cited, so completeness must be scored separately from correctness.
Unit tests for data loaders should check missing fields and duplicate passage ids.
